lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 114, which lets you rename a file right where its name is shown.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one fourteen, which lets you rename a file right where its name is shown.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
A new preference, on by default, makes F2 in the details view edit the file's name in the list.
You press F2, or choose Rename, on one selected file in the details view.
If the row is out of view, Thunar scrolls to it, then waits for an idle moment.
The Name cell turns into a text entry, with the name selected but not its extension.
Enter renames through the dialog's own job, so undo and error dialogs still work; Escape cancels.
The icon and compact views, or the preference turned off, open the rename popover from issue 15.
lines.say: The icon and compact views, or the preference turned off, open the rename popover from issue fifteen.

lines.caption: Launchers, renames over D-Bus and bulk renames keep their dialogs.
lines.say: Launchers, renames over D Bus and bulk renames keep their dialogs.

lines.caption: Thunar always renamed in a separate box, while Nemo and most file managers edit the name in place.
Thunar already had the code to edit a name in its row; nothing ever asked for it until now.
The action manager checks the preference, that the file isn't a launcher, and that this is the details view.
Editing starts only after the scroll has been drawn, so the entry lands on the row.
The entry opens in the Name column wherever you've moved it, not just the first column.
An empty name, one with a slash, or one over 255 bytes keeps the entry open; switching window keeps your text.
lines.say: An empty name, one with a slash, or one over two hundred fifty-five bytes keeps the entry open; switching window keeps your text.

lines.caption: If editing can't start, the popover opens instead, but only while the view still shows the file's folder.
The launcher question, the D-Bus dialog and Rename Multiple Files are unchanged.
lines.say: The launcher question, the D Bus dialog and Rename Multiple Files are unchanged.

lines.caption: Enter or a click elsewhere renames, and Ctrl+Z renames it back; a click with a bad name keeps the error; Escape cancels.
lines.say: Enter or a click elsewhere renames, and control Z renames it back; a click with a bad name keeps the error; Escape cancels.

lines.caption: A bad or too long name shows an error icon; a taken name shows Thunar's rename error and the old name stays.
When GTK closes the entry itself, editing starts again on that row with your text and its selection kept.
Switching window, or a progress or error dialog, keeps the entry open with your text; nothing is renamed until you confirm.
Closing the tab cancels, so a half-typed name is never saved.
In the details view, the entry sits exactly in the Name cell.
The icon and compact views use a widget from libexo that puts the entry in the wrong place.
lines.say: The icon and compact views use a widget from lib exo that puts the entry in the wrong place.

lines.caption: The issue allows that, so those views fall back to the popover.
Most of the code is in the standard view; the dialog, popover and in-place rename now share one rename function.
To get the old behavior back, untick Rename files in place in the Behavior tab of Preferences.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was built and tested locally; CI's two reviews found 17 problems, 13 fixed and 4 small ones accepted.
lines.say: It was built and tested locally; C I's two reviews found seventeen problems, thirteen fixed and four small ones accepted.

lines.caption: It builds on Thunar's unused editing code, the rename dialog's job, and the popover from issue 15.
lines.say: It builds on Thoonar's unused editing code, the rename dialog's job, and the popover from issue fifteen.

lines.caption: Every local result ran before CI's review fixes, and none was re-run after them.
The package was built from git, as CI does, and Thunar passed the smoke test.
This PR's test renamed in place, undid it, and checked Escape, bad names and a taken name.
It also checked scrolling, a moved Name column, the context menu, and every fallback.
The tests for issues 15 and 96 still pass.
lines.say: The tests for issues fifteen and ninety-six still pass.

lines.caption: The other tests ran only at the first commit, not after the later fixes.
A screenshot audit found two problems, both fixed; the final shots are audited after CI's run.
None of CI's review fixes were built or tested locally; the newest wait for the next CI run.
A local code review found six problems; three are fixed, two are left as they are, and one is this page.
The biggest fix: a cancel started by GTK no longer saves a half-typed name.
Left as is: no length check in the entry, and Ctrl+Z while typing undoes a file operation, as in the popover.
lines.say: Left as is: no length check in the entry, and control Z while typing undoes a file operation, as in the popover.

lines.caption: Then CI reviewed the first push and found eight problems; CI fixed six itself, and the building session fixed the other two.
The biggest: switching window or closing the tab mid-edit no longer saves a half-typed name.
And when GTK cancels the edit itself, editing restarts on the row with your text kept.
Four smaller fixes guard the popover fallback, scroll to the Name column, share one rename function, and drop a comment.
The last two clear a pending rename when the view closes and refuse names over 255 bytes.
lines.say: The last two clear a pending rename when the view closes and refuse names over two hundred fifty-five bytes.

lines.caption: CI's second review found nine more problems; five are fixed, and those fixes wait for CI's next run.
Closing a tab no longer saves a half-typed name, a restarted edit keeps its selection, and expanded folders are found.
Alt+Tab or a dialog no longer drops your typed name: editing restarts with it, and nothing is renamed until you confirm.
A click elsewhere with a bad name now keeps the entry open, so the error shows.
Four small, unconfirmed findings are accepted rather than fixed, as the repo's review rules allow.
One can't happen, and the other scrolls to the Name column, which is the right target.
The name check has no library function to reuse, and the repeated check guards a different branch.
CI's build, tests and review of the newest fixes, and the screenshot audit, come with the next CI run.
Daily use on your own desktop comes after the merge.
Links to the pull request and CI's first run are at the end of Part 2.
CI's second run, with its second review, is linked there too.
After the merge, select a file in the details view and press F2.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue builds on this one yet.
Once this is merged, try F2 in your own folders.
A possible follow-up would fix the icon views' editing, so they can rename in place too.
That fix is in libexo; the rename code here is already shared by every view.
lines.say: That fix is in lib exo; the rename code here is already shared by every view.

lines.caption: In short: F2 now renames right in the list, and every other case keeps the box you know.
